summary: Joined node1, node2, node3 into a single RabbitMQ 4.3.5 cluster (Erlang 27.3.4.17), created the `payments` vhost with an app user `payments_app` granted full permissions, and a durable quorum queue `orders` replicated across all three nodes. Verified messages published to the queue survive the loss of the leader node and remain consumable from a surviving node. Completed the mandatory sequential restart of all three nodes with boot-id-verified reboots and post-restart cluster/queue health checks.
actions_performed: Installed erlang 27.3.4.17 (from rabbitmq/erlang-rpm GitHub release) and rabbitmq-server 4.3.5 (from rabbitmq/rabbitmq-server GitHub release) on node1, node2, node3 (AlmaLinux 9.6)
Populated /etc/hosts with CLUSTER_HOSTS on all nodes, set a shared Erlang cookie in /var/lib/rabbitmq/.erlang.cookie
Opened firewalld ports 4369, 5672, 15672, 25672, 35672-35682 on all three nodes (previously blocking inter-node clustering)
Enabled+started rabbitmq-server and rabbitmq_management plugin on all nodes
Joined node2 and node3 into a single cluster with node1 as seed via rabbitmqctl join_cluster; verified cluster_status shows 3 running disk nodes with no partitions
Created vhost 'payments', user 'payments_app' (generated random password via openssl, passed only via secret_env) with full configure/write/read permissions on that vhost
Declared durable quorum queue 'orders' in vhost payments via a pika/AMQP script (installed python3-pip + pika), replicated across all 3 nodes
Published 5 durable messages, verified queue held 5 messages with leader on node1

Stopped rabbitmq-server on node1 (the queue leader) to simulate node loss; confirmed quorum queue elected new leader (node3) and retained all 5 messages; consumed all 5 messages successfully from node3
Restarted node1's rabbitmq-server and confirmed cluster returned to 3/3 running nodes, no partitions, quorum queue back to 3 members
Captured pre-restart boot_id and RabbitMQ health baseline on all 3 nodes
Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 via systemctl reboot (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect), polled each until reachable, and confirmed boot_id changed on each

After each reboot, confirmed rabbitmq-server became active and cluster_status showed all 3 nodes running with no network partitions and the quorum queue with all 3 members before proceeding to the next node
After all 3 restarts, did a final end-to-end publish (from node1) and consume (from node3) of 5 durable messages to confirm full data-path integrity post-restart

evidence.summary: cluster_status on node1 shows Disk Nodes and Running Nodes = rabbit@node1, rabbit@node2, rabbit@node3, no network partitions

evidence.requirement: payments vhost + application account with publish/consume rights
evidence.summary: add_vhost payments, add_user payments_app, set_permissions .* .* .* on payments; replicated metadata confirmed visible via list_vhosts/list_users on node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: Durable queue replicated across nodes (quorum queue)
evidence.summary: Declared durable quorum queue 'orders' via AMQP; list_queues shows type=quorum, durable=true, members = node1+node2+node3

evidence.requirement: Messages survive loss of one node and remain consumable from remaining nodes
evidence.summary: 5 durable messages published and confirmed in queue; node1 (queue leader) stopped; queue re-elected leader to node3 while retaining 5 messages; all 5 messages consumed successfully from node3 while node1 was down

evidence.requirement: Recovery after restoring the disrupted node / final cluster health
evidence.summary: node1 rabbitmq-server restarted, cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running again with quorum queue back to 3 members and zero network partitions

Baseline boot_id 54089086-...; systemctl reboot issued and acked; node briefly unreachable; new boot_id 40e78070-... confirms actual reboot; post-restart cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running, quorum queue with 3 members, no partitions

Baseline boot_id e65e6bcf-...; reboot issued and acked; node briefly unreachable; new boot_id 5c6df6ce-... confirms reboot; post-restart rabbitmq-server active and cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running

Baseline boot_id 8c28f3cd-...; reboot issued and acked; node briefly unreachable; new boot_id f9f653a1-... confirms reboot; rabbitmq-server active afterward; cluster_status confirms all 3 nodes running, no partitions, quorum queue with 3 members (node3 in Running Nodes confirmed via extended sed range)

evidence.requirement: Final end-to-end functional proof after all restarts
evidence.summary: Published 5 fresh durable messages from node1 and consumed all 5 from node3 after all three nodes had been sequentially rebooted, confirming full cluster/data functionality post-restart
